subject: On-prem cluster sizing and HA storage checklist
messages:
From: Elena Romero <elena.romero@acme-retail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-team@acme-retail.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: on-prem cluster sizing for Redwood Private deployment

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this. We're starting planning for an on-prem deployment of Redwood Private in our primary data center (us-west-2-equivalent). High level: we expect ~15 steady concurrent inference sessions (chat/generation) with occasional batch embedding jobs for nightly indexing. The business wants an HA control plane and a resilient storage layer that survives node restarts.

Can you send a short checklist of cluster requirements, recommended node pool layout (CPU/GPU mix), and storage options (PVC, CSI, recommended sizes)? Also any network requirements (eg. load balancer, NAT, firewall rules) we should include in our procurement ticket.

If helpful, I can share our current cluster spec and contact details for SRE. We'd like a first pass by end of week so the procurement ticket can include hardware specs.

Thanks,
Elena

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: on-prem cluster sizing for Redwood Private deployment

Elena —

Appreciate the context. Attaching a short sizing worksheet and a network diagram template to make it concrete (acme-cluster-sizing.xlsx, acme-network-diagram.png). Quick summary of what we typically recommend for a production-ready on-prem Redwood Private install:

- Control plane: 3 management nodes (kube control-plane) in three AZs/racks where possible for etcd stability.
- Inference node pools: separate CPU pool for small low-latency requests and GPU pool for large models/batch workloads.
- GPU config: NVIDIA 48GB A40 / A100 class recommended for medium models; 2–4 GPUs per node depending on your rack power.
- Storage: fast SSD-backed block storage for model artifacts + an object-store-compatible layer (S3 gateway or MinIO) for backups and immutable artifacts.
- Network: dedicated VLAN, egress through a NAT gateway, allow inbound from Redwood control plane IPs (we'll provide), cluster CIDR-based firewall rules, and an L4 load balancer in front of the inference service for L7 routing.

A few clarifying questions before I finalize the checklist:
1) Do you have an existing cluster (k8s 1.24+) or are we installing a new one?
2) Expected peak token throughput (tokens/sec) or QPS for text generation — helps sizing GPU counts.
3) Any procurement constraints (only 2U servers, no GPUs >16GB, etc.)?

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute tech sync tomorrow.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Architect – Private Deployments

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Romero <elena.romero@acme-retail.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: on-prem cluster sizing for Redwood Private deployment

Elena / team —

Following up with a technical checklist and concrete node pool suggestions based on common Acme-like workloads. I kept the assumptions conservative: 15 concurrent chat sessions (each ~60 tokens/s peak) and nightly batch embedding of ~25 million embeddings over 4 hours. Adjust as you provide exact QPS/token numbers.

Checklist (high level):
- Kubernetes: 1.27+ recommended, RBAC enabled, pod-security policies or OPA/Gatekeeper for onboarding.
- Control plane: 3 x m8.large style (8 vCPU / 32GB) dedicated for k8s control-plane + etcd. Anti-affinity across racks.
- Node pools:
  * inference-cpu: 4 x c8-standard (16 vCPU / 64GB) — run proxy, light transformer quantized models, preprocessing, batching services.
  * inference-gpu-small: 2 x GPU nodes (NVIDIA A10 or A30, 24–48GB) for mid-size models and burst traffic.
  * inference-gpu-large: 2 x GPU nodes (A40 / A100 class, 48+ GB) for heavy models / dedicated throughput.
  * batch-workers: 3 x c16-large (32 vCPU / 128GB) for embedding indexing jobs (cron jobs + K8s jobs).
- Autoscaling: Cluster-autoscaler with node taints and pod tolerations; set conservative scale-up (1–2 nodes) for rapid bursts.
- Storage:
  * Model volumes: Read-mostly, use a fast block CSI (NVMe or SSD backing). Recommended PV size per model: 20–200GB depending on model family. Keep a hot cache layer (local NVMe) for active models.
  * Persistent data: Use replicated distributed filesystem for smaller metadata (e.g., CephFS) or object-store for large artifacts.
  * Backups: Weekly snapshot to S3-compatible endpoint; daily incremental.
  * PVCs: Use storage classes with reclaimPolicy=Retain for model artifacts; set IO limits via CSI.
- Networking:
  * CNI: Calico or Cilium with strict network policies.
  * LB: External L4 (HAProxy or MetalLB) + internal L7 (ingress controller) for tenant routing.
  * Egress: NAT gateway and DNS allowlist for outbound to Redwood control plane and SSO provider.
  * Ports: 443 for API, 50051 for internal gRPC (or configured ports).
- Security:
  * KMS integration for model encryption at rest.
  * Audit logging forwarded to SIEM.
  * Service accounts with least privilege.

Sizing rationale / numbers:
- For 15 concurrent low-latency sessions, 2 x 48GB GPUs (A40) should handle baseline with room to spare when combined with batching and KV cache.
- Embedding throughput: use batch-workers with CPU instances; parallelize across 8–16 pods.

Attachments: I updated acme-cluster-sizing.xlsx with node counts and rough cost estimates. Also included a simple network-diagram png.

Next steps:
1) Elena: confirm QPS/tokens and any hardware constraints.
2) Redwood: send ip ranges and recommended firewall rules, plus a proposed install weekend window.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: SRE Lead <sre_lead@acme-retail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Romero <elena.romero@acme-retail.com>, dev.patel@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: on-prem cluster sizing for Redwood Private deployment

Evelyn / Dev —

Thanks for the detailed checklist and concrete node pool recommendations. This is exactly what procurement needed. A few quick confirmations from our side:
- We can provide 2U nodes with A40-equivalent GPUs (48GB) in the primary rack; power limits verified.
- We have an existing k8s 1.26 cluster but prefer a fresh cluster for isolation; we'll follow your 1.27+ suggestion.
- Backup target: we will provide an S3-compatible endpoint in our off-site DR region.

Procurement will include the following line items per your sheet: 2 x A40 nodes (inference-gpu-large), 2 x A30 nodes (inference-gpu-small), 4 x CPU nodes for CPU pool, and 3 control-plane VMs.

Next steps from Acme: I'll open the procurement ticket by EOD and share the PO number here. Please send your firewall IP ranges and the install playbook link so we can schedule an install weekend (targeting Jun 12–13).

Acceptance: we accept the sizing recommendations as the starting point. Please send the DocuSign SOW for signature when you have the install playbook finalized.

Best,
SRE Lead
Acme Retail
